    cliEnv() hardcodes /dev/null for git config isolation. This will break when running integration tests on non-Unix platforms (and is avoidable even on Unix). Consider using os.DevNull (and constructing the env entry as GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM= + os.DevNull) so the null device path is correct for the current OS.

        "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0",           // Prevent interactive prompts from blocking in tests
        "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null", // Isolate from user's global git config (e.g. global gitignore)
        "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null", // Isolate from system git config

cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/testenv.go:121

    cliEnv() uses append(os.Environ(), ...) to add GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM. If either variable is already present in the parent environment, this can produce duplicate keys; many programs (via getenv) will read the first occurrence, so the intended override may not take effect and git config could still leak into tests. Filter out existing GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM entries (or build a map and re-flatten) before appending to guarantee the override works.

    return append(os.Environ(),
        "ENTIRE_TEST_CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR="+env.ClaudeProjectDir,
        "ENTIRE_TEST_GEMINI_PROJECT_DIR="+env.GeminiProjectDir,
        "ENTIRE_TEST_OPENCODE_PROJECT_DIR="+env.OpenCodeProjectDir,
        "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY=0",           // Prevent interactive prompts from blocking in tests
        "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null", // Isolate from user's global git config (e.g. global gitignore)
        "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null", // Isolate from system git config
